subject: English
q: Employees were given extra leave in lieu ______ overtime pay.
explanation: The phrase is ‘in lieu of’, meaning ‘instead of’.

subject: English
q: With regard ______ your application, we are pleased to inform you that it has been accepted.
explanation: The fixed phrase is ‘with regard to’.

subject: English
q: Owing ______ bad weather, the flight was cancelled.
explanation: ‘Owing to’ means ‘because of’.

subject: English
q: He signed the agreement on behalf ______ the company.
explanation: The phrase is ‘on behalf of’, meaning ‘as the representative of’.

subject: English
q: He was appointed to the board by virtue ______ his long experience.
explanation: ‘By virtue of’ means ‘because of’ or ‘on the strength of’.

subject: English
q: In view ______ the rising number of cases, schools will remain closed.
explanation: ‘In view of’ means ‘considering’.

subject: English
q: Early explorers set out in quest ______ new trade routes.
explanation: The phrase is ‘in quest of’, meaning ‘in search of’.

subject: English
q: The match was postponed on account ______ rain.
explanation: ‘On account of’ means ‘because of’.

subject: English
q: The reforms were carried through in the teeth ______ fierce opposition.
explanation: The idiom ‘in the teeth of’ means ‘in spite of strong opposition’.

subject: English
q: Small farmers are often at the mercy ______ moneylenders.
explanation: The phrase is ‘at the mercy of’.

subject: English
q: Pakistan came into being ______ 14 August 1947.
explanation: ‘On’ is used with days and dates.

subject: English
q: The Quaid-e-Azam was born ______ 1876.
explanation: ‘In’ is used with years, months and seasons.

subject: English
q: The Karachi express leaves ______ 6.45 p.m.
explanation: ‘At’ is used with clock times.

subject: English
q: Please submit the assignment ______ Friday; late work will not be accepted.
explanation: ‘By’ marks a deadline (not later than); ‘until’ marks a period that continues up to a point.

subject: English
q: On Sundays the shops remain closed ______ noon.
explanation: ‘Until’ is used for a state that continues up to a certain time.

subject: English
q: Nobody is allowed to leave the hall ______ the examination.
explanation: ‘During’ is a preposition used before a noun for a period; ‘while’ is a conjunction introducing a clause.

subject: English
q: The project must be completed ______ six months.
explanation: ‘Within’ means ‘before the end of’ a stated period.

subject: English
q: I usually go for a walk ______ the evening.
explanation: We say ‘in the morning/afternoon/evening’.

subject: English
q: The main bazaar stays open late ______ night.
explanation: The fixed expression is ‘at night’ (but ‘in the night’).

subject: English
q: The sweets were distributed ______ the children of the village.
explanation: ‘Among’ is used when sharing is spread over more than two people.

subject: English
q: Our office is ______ the third floor.
explanation: We say ‘on the first/second/third floor’.

subject: English
q: He jumped ______ the river to save the drowning child.
explanation: ‘Into’ shows movement from outside to inside.

subject: English
q: The frightened cat climbed ______ the roof.
explanation: ‘Onto’ shows movement to a position on a surface.

subject: English
q: In class he always sits ______ his best friend.
explanation: ‘Beside’ means ‘next to’; ‘besides’ means ‘in addition to’.

subject: English
q: ______ English, she speaks French and Arabic.
explanation: ‘Besides’ means ‘in addition to’; ‘beside’ means ‘next to’.

subject: English
q: Most students come to college ______ bus.
explanation: ‘By’ is used for means of transport without an article (by bus, by train).

subject: English
q: The boat sailed ______ the coast from Karachi to Gwadar.
explanation: ‘Along’ means following the length of something.

subject: English
q: A new car is ______ my means at present.
explanation: The idiom is ‘beyond one’s means’, i.e. more than one can afford.

subject: English
q: The minister is accountable ______ Parliament ______ the use of public funds.
explanation: One is accountable to a person or body for one’s actions.

subject: English
q: The treaty put an end ______ decades ______ hostility.
explanation: The phrase is ‘put an end to’; ‘decades of’ expresses quantity of time.

subject: English
q: She was appointed ______ the post ______ merit.
explanation: One is appointed to a post, and selection is made on merit.

subject: English
q: The report throws light ______ the causes ______ the decline in exports.
explanation: The idiom is ‘throw light on’; ‘cause of’ names what is caused.

subject: English
q: She is married ______ a doctor and lives ______ Hyderabad.
explanation: One is married to a person; ‘in’ is used with cities.

subject: English
q: The student was expelled ______ the college ______ misconduct.
explanation: One is expelled from an institution for an offence.

subject: English
q: The Chinese delegation arrived ______ Islamabad ______ Monday morning.
explanation: One arrives in a city; ‘on’ is used with a named day, including ‘Monday morning’.

subject: English
q: There is no substitute ______ hard work and no shortcut ______ success.
explanation: ‘Substitute’ takes ‘for’, and ‘shortcut’ takes ‘to’.

subject: English
q: The judge took notice ______ the delay and ordered an inquiry ______ the matter.
explanation: The phrase is ‘take notice of’, and an investigation is an ‘inquiry into’ something.

subject: English
q: The by-election was marred ______ violence, which cast doubt ______ the result.
explanation: Something is marred by a fault; one casts doubt on (or upon) something.

subject: English
q: His family emigrated ______ Pakistan ______ Canada in the 1990s.
explanation: People emigrate from one country to another.

subject: English
q: Regardless ______ the cost, the government pressed ahead ______ the project.
explanation: The phrase is ‘regardless of’, and one ‘presses ahead with’ a plan.

subject: English
q: Mr Farooq is known to be ______ honest officer.
explanation: ‘Honest’ begins with a vowel sound because the h is silent, so it takes ‘an’.

subject: English
q: The journey from Rawalpindi to the airport took half ______ hour.
explanation: ‘Hour’ has a silent h and begins with a vowel sound, so the phrase is ‘half an hour’.

subject: English
q: She was the first woman in her family to earn ______ university degree.
explanation: ‘University’ begins with a consonant sound /j/ (‘yoo’), so it takes ‘a’.

subject: English
q: You cannot turn left here because this is ______ one-way street.
explanation: ‘One’ is pronounced with an initial /w/ sound, so it takes ‘a’.

subject: English
q: She is studying for ______ MBA at a private university in Lahore.
explanation: The letter M is pronounced ‘em’, which begins with a vowel sound, so ‘an’ is used.

subject: English
q: He works for ______ NGO that runs schools in Tharparkar.
explanation: The letter N is pronounced ‘en’, beginning with a vowel sound, so the abbreviation takes ‘an’.

subject: English
q: The driver made ______ U-turn in the middle of the road.
explanation: The letter U is pronounced ‘yoo’, beginning with a consonant sound, so it takes ‘a’.

subject: English
q: Before the operation, the patient had to have ______ X-ray.
explanation: The letter X is pronounced ‘eks’, beginning with a vowel sound, so it takes ‘an’.

subject: English
q: The internship gave her ______ unique opportunity to see Parliament at work.
explanation: ‘Unique’ begins with the consonant sound /j/, so it takes ‘a’, not ‘an’.

subject: English
q: The police registered ______ FIR against the driver.
explanation: The letter F is pronounced ‘ef’, beginning with a vowel sound, so ‘an FIR’ is correct.

subject: English
q: After a long debate the committee reached ______ unanimous decision.
explanation: ‘Unanimous’ is pronounced ‘yoo-nanimous’, with a consonant sound, so it takes ‘a’.

subject: English
q: At the seminar I met ______ American and ______ European.
explanation: ‘American’ begins with a vowel sound (an), while ‘European’ begins with the consonant sound /j/ (a).

subject: English
q: Everyone knows that ______ honesty is the best policy.
explanation: Abstract nouns used in a general sense take no article.

subject: English
q: The boys play ______ hockey every evening.
explanation: Names of games and sports take no article.

subject: English
q: My younger brother goes to ______ school by van.
explanation: When an institution is visited for its main purpose (a pupil attending lessons), no article is used.

subject: English
q: Her father went to ______ school to meet the headmistress.
explanation: When a place like a school is visited for another purpose, it is a particular building and takes ‘the’.

subject: English
q: He usually has ______ breakfast at seven.
explanation: Names of meals used in a general sense take no article.

subject: English
q: ______ breakfast we had at the hotel was excellent.
explanation: A meal defined by a following clause is specific, so it takes ‘the’.

subject: English
q: ______ life is full of surprises.
explanation: ‘Life’ in a general, abstract sense takes no article.

subject: English
q: ______ life of the Quaid-e-Azam is an example for us all.
explanation: An abstract noun made specific by an ‘of’ phrase takes ‘the’.

subject: English
q: She speaks ______ Urdu and English fluently.
explanation: Names of languages take no article (unless followed by ‘language’).

subject: English
q: ______ Mount Everest was first climbed in 1953.
explanation: Names of single mountain peaks take no article, unlike mountain ranges.

subject: English
q: He was elected ______ chairman of the standing committee.
explanation: A unique title or post used after verbs such as elect or appoint normally takes no article.

subject: English
q: ______ water boils at 100 °C at sea level.
explanation: Material nouns used in a general sense take no article.

subject: English
q: ______ water in this pond is not fit for drinking.
explanation: A material noun made specific by a phrase (in this pond) takes ‘the’.

subject: English
q: ______ Pakistan is largely an agricultural country.
explanation: Most singular country names take no article.

subject: English
q: The children went to ______ bed at nine o’clock.
explanation: In ‘go to bed’ the bed is used for its purpose, so no article is used.

subject: English
q: His uncle has been in ______ prison for fraud since last year.
explanation: When prison is used for its main purpose (being an inmate), no article is used.

subject: English
q: The rescue team reached the village by ______ nightfall.
explanation: Times of day such as nightfall, dawn and sunset take no article after ‘by’ or ‘at’.

subject: English
q: ______ Sun is the nearest star to the Earth.
explanation: Things that are unique take ‘the’.

subject: English
q: K2 is ______ second-highest mountain in the world.
explanation: Ordinal numbers and superlatives take ‘the’.

subject: English
q: Ali is ______ tallest boy in the class.
explanation: A superlative adjective before a noun takes ‘the’.

subject: English
q: Hameed was ______ first to reach the scene of the accident.
explanation: ‘First’ used as an ordinal (the first person) takes ‘the’.

subject: English
q: Ayesha plays ______ violin in the college orchestra.
explanation: In British usage, musical instruments take ‘the’ after ‘play’.

subject: English
q: The new tax is meant to ensure that ______ rich pay their fair share.
explanation: ‘The’ plus an adjective (the rich, the poor) denotes a whole class of people.

subject: English
q: ______ Chinese built the Great Wall to protect their northern frontier.
explanation: Nationality adjectives ending in -ese, -sh or -ch take ‘the’ when they refer to the whole people.

subject: English
q: ______ Holy Quran was revealed over a period of about twenty-three years.
explanation: Names of sacred books take ‘the’.

subject: English
q: ______ Prime Minister will address the nation tonight.
explanation: A unique office referred to as a known post takes ‘the’.

subject: English
q: ______ news of his promotion spread quickly.
explanation: ‘News’ is uncountable and never takes ‘a’; here it is specific, so ‘the’ is used.

subject: English
q: In the old city, eggs are still sold by ______ dozen.
explanation: After ‘by’ in expressions of measurement (by the dozen, by the kilo), ‘the’ is used.
